target_customer: Teams and knowledge workers who want to find what AI can automate in their own work
problem: Teams want to adopt AI but do not know where to start. A desktop app uses local models over email, docs, Slack, calendar, browser and file history to find the highest value automations per employee.
business_model: Desktop software for teams, pricing not public

founders.name: Anshul Paul
prior_employers: HappyRobot (founding team, grew to 100 plus employees, Seed to Series B)
founders.background_notes: YC page says he worked on AI evals and observability at HappyRobot.

founders.name: Vaibhav Agrawal
founders.background_notes: Named as co-founder on the YC launch post; the YC company page names him only in a post about Clam.

technical_complexity.rationale: Mining local history across many apps and running local models on user machines is standard engineering with hard privacy and quality parts.

defensibility.rationale: Task mining is an established category and big platforms can add the feature. Little proprietary data or lock in.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: These vendors already sold task mining; roundups list them as alternatives. The company later launched a different product, Clam, in February 2026.

market_need_then: Companies are pressed to adopt AI but lack guidance on where; the task mining market is described as about 2 billion USD in 2025 by a vendor roundup. No dated customer evidence for this product.

branding.domain_note: Uses baseframe.co, not a .com. The site showed a coming soon page.

brand_strength.rationale: No brand coverage found, and the same name was used for a hardware design copilot on a YC launch post, so the identity is muddled.

pivots.from: BaseFrame product (automation discovery per the YC page; a hardware design copilot per a YC launch post)
pivots.to: Clam, a security product for broad access AI agents
pivots.why: Not stated; reported by a Yespress profile and the Clam post on the YC page

outcome_analysis: BaseFrame is an Active Winter 2026 YC company with two founders. Sources disagree on its product, showing automation discovery and a hardware design copilot, and it appears to have moved to a new product, Clam, in February 2026. Funding beyond the YC deal was not found, so the outcome is open.
notes: A Yespress profile reports a 130K USD seed from Y Combinator in January 2026, from an aggregator only and the standard YC deal, so not recorded as a round. Product identity conflict: YC page text says desktop automation discovery; a YC launch post and Crunchbase describe hardware design scoping. Competitor list empty because task mining roundups were undated. Outcome search found no news. The recorded 130K seed rests on a single outlet (Yespress) and is probably the standard YC deal.
